findings.title: Spring for GraphQL Unsafe Deserialization in pagination support
findings.summary_md: Spring's advisory for CVE-2026-59285, published August 20, 2026, describes unsafe deserialization when a Spring for GraphQL application processes paginated GraphQL queries. Spring says exploitation requires Spring GraphQL, Jackson 2.x for JSON deserialization, an exposed paginated Connection field, and specific classes on the classpath that can execute unintended logic during instantiation or deserialization. Affected versions are Spring for GraphQL 2.0.0 through 2.0.4; the listed fixes are 2.0.5 for OSS and 2.0.4.1 for Enterprise Support. The advisory rates the issue HIGH and lists no further mitigation steps beyond upgrading.

findings.title: Spring Security embedded UnboundID LDAP server exposes well-known administrative bind DN on all network interfaces
findings.summary_md: Spring's August 20, 2026 advisory for CVE-2026-59270 says the embedded UnboundID LDAP server in Spring Security registers an administrative credential unconditionally and binds its listener to all available network interfaces. An attacker who can reach the LDAP port can authenticate with a well-known administrative bind DN and then read or modify entries in the in-memory directory. The advisory lists affected Spring Security lines from 5.7.0 through 7.1.0 and fixes including 7.1.1 OSS, 7.0.7 OSS, and enterprise-only releases for older branches. It rates the flaw CRITICAL.

findings.title: 91 Spring CVEs Highlight the Growing AI Vulnerability Consumption Problem
findings.summary_md: Sonatype's August 21, 2026 post says Broadcom published a large batch of Spring security advisories on August 20 and that Sonatype tracked 91 CVEs across Spring Framework and related projects. At publication, Sonatype Guide reported 148,608 affected software components, many of them non-Spring components bundling vulnerable Spring code. The post singles out CVE-2026-59285 in Spring for GraphQL as 9.2 Critical and CVE-2026-59318 in Spring AI as a Medium-severity tool-calling boundary issue. It recommends mapping affected versions across applications and repositories and moving them to fixed releases.
